correctness.rationale: For an unfilled graph complex, every face through size t+1 is automatic and faces of size t+2 are precisely the sets containing a graph edge. In the augmented exterior chain model the degree-t cycle lattice is wedge^{t+1} U for the vertex augmentation kernel U. For a fixed edge uv, all top-simplex boundaries using that edge span (e_v-e_u) wedge wedge^t U, using the basis of differences from u. Consequently, if E is the edge-difference lattice, lower homology is naturally wedge^{t+1}(U/E); the latter quotient lattice is the component augmentation kernel. This proves saturation and automorphism naturality. Full-skeleton exactness below t, top boundary rank, and Pascal's identity give the asserted remaining groups and multiplicities, including simplex cases. Finally, over a wedge of t-spheres, Hurewicz identifies attaching maps with their integral degree vectors; for t>=2 changes of bases of the two sphere wedges are realized by homotopy equivalences. Unit Smith factors cancel in the mapping cone, leaving exactly the two sphere dimensions. Independent integral signed-boundary examples reproduce the path, cycle, mixed-group example, larger tolerances, and a simplex case.
residual_risks: t=1, filled cliques and equivariant homotopy are not asserted. The finite reproduction does not prove the uniform theorem; the exterior model and attaching argument do.
